entries.title: Consume route commands after the destination has accepted them
entries.trigger: a nested destination converts URL parameters into local work and clears the URL.
entries.mechanism: clearing parameters during the incoming navigation commit was lost or dispatched through the previous focused route. A query gated on cleared parameters never started. A hook test with synchronous local parameter setters did not model this failure. A retained sibling destination can also process a new route command while still unfocused; its ordinary leave cleanup can then erase the accepted state before focus and bypass dismissal side effects such as camera restoration.
entries.prevention: accept the command into local state, then consume its parameters through the destination's own navigation object after that state commits. Use the existing return/dismiss API when revisiting an existing screen; opening another copy retains extra native surfaces and history. Match the action to the targeted navigator: Expo Router 57.0.19 dispatches dismissTo as POP_TO, which nested ordinary tabs do not handle. Navigate within tabs and dismiss only from the covering stack screen. When the command owns immediate visible destination state, require destination focus before accepting or consuming it; do not let a retained hidden screen create state that its unfocused cleanup removes.
verification: use real stack/drawer/tab navigators for retained and cold destinations; assert that the real consumer starts its query, applies its result and retains exactly one destination. Native gesture responsiveness is a separate physical check. Include external entry while the destination is already focused and while a sibling tab is selected; for the retained case, assert that the command remains pending while hidden and is accepted exactly once after focus. Entry from a covering screen is insufficient.
boundaries: 2026-09-12, Expo Router 57.0.19 / React 19.2.3; the original implementation failed route and retained-focus fixtures, while scoped consumption after destination acceptance passed with the actual query hooks.

entries.title: End temporary entry context at its terminal success
entries.trigger: an external notification or deep link creates temporary destination state around a refreshable remote query.
entries.mechanism: a successful map-viewport fit left its notification context mounted. After a related view removed the final remote member, foreground refetch interpreted the old command as a newly unavailable entry and displayed false failure feedback.
entries.prevention: define the command's terminal success independently from later domain mutations and clear its temporary context when that success is accepted. Retain context only for actionable partial, unavailable or retry states. Dismissing its feedback must end the context too.
verification: complete the entry, mutate or expire its backing row, then background and resume the retained destination. The completed entry must not refetch or produce new feedback; initial empty, filtered and failed controls must remain available.
boundaries: 2026-09-08, React Native 0.86.3 / TanStack Query 5.101.4; the focused hook regression passed.

entries.title: Visible consumers must adopt useful in-flight preparation
entries.trigger: a background producer prepares immutable media for a foreground consumer that uses the same stable cache identity, especially across navigation or focus changes.
entries.mechanism: the producer started downloading the consumer's first images, but visible mount treated foreground priority as permission to abort the matching transfer. The foreground request then restarted from zero while unrelated background transfers completed, so the first visible image could display last. A unit test asserted the abort and stayed green because it described the implementation, not the intended handoff. Candidate selection can cause the same user-visible miss when preparation follows producer presentation order instead of the consumer's first-window order. Even after handoff is preserved, eagerly mounted consumers can bypass a bounded scheduler by starting their own native transports for queued keys; the nominal concurrency limit then does not bound actual network work.
entries.prevention: identify work by immutable media and authorization owner. Prepare the exact first bounded consumer window before focus. If matching work is already running, let the consumer adopt it without abort or a second download and publish the completed stable cache entry as its placeholder. Start a direct foreground request when matching work is only queued: the visible consumer outranks speculative lookahead and suppresses that duplicate task. If matching work is already running, adopt it instead. Track whether a mounted consumer is waiting or direct so offscreen mounts do not bypass the background limit and visible direct mounts suppress duplicate speculation. Continue to cancel obsolete identities, owners and unclaimed work.
verification: hold the first preparation promise, mount the consumer, change producer focus and assert that the original signal remains active and the download count stays one. Complete the write, verify that the consumer receives the stable cached source and reaches native display, then prove an unrelated task is still cancelled. With N slots, prove an offscreen N+1 consumer waits, while the same consumer marked actually visible renders its ready URL immediately and prevents the duplicate queued task from starting after a slot opens. Assert the exact visible IDs, first-window IDs and scroll-ahead order separately. Demonstrate that the regression fails with the old behavior, then verify cold cache on the affected device.
boundaries: 2026-09-08, Expo Image 57.0.4 and React 19.2. Physical iOS exposed both missing transition coverage and queue bypass; a clean-device feed pass and compact-to-large-to-compact profile-image path were accepted after correction. Other lifecycle and replacement paths remain separate.

entries.title: Versioned bytes and their identity must travel together
entries.trigger: profile/content rows and signed image URLs refresh independently while native caches use immutable entity/version keys.
entries.mechanism: a fresh profile version is combined with an old signed URL. Native display then stores old bytes under the new version, or a removed image returns from retained URL metadata.
entries.prevention: select a remote source only when its own version matches the requested content version. Keep source metadata together during merges; content-photo equality does not imply profile-image equality.
verification: delay URL renewal after a profile replacement/removal. Inspect the actual image source and cache key, then supply matching metadata and confirm ordinary display and cross-surface reuse.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Expo Image 57.0.4. Native cache persistence needs device evidence separately.

entries.title: Expiring state must recover after resume
entries.trigger: mounted React Native screens with expiring remote data or signed media URLs.
entries.mechanism: a network subscription can update online state while application focus never reaches the query layer. After a long lock, stale rows or URLs remain until manual refresh.
entries.prevention: integrate application focus and connectivity independently using the query library's supported interfaces. Decide what must refresh on resume and preserve bounded request ownership. A mounted screen is not necessarily focused; a focused screen is not necessarily online. Check current AppState when installing or rerunning effects too; a session/connectivity update during background must not restart foreground-only work before another AppState event arrives. Retaining a dismissed sheet's content for its exit animation must not keep its queries polling. Express query activity separately from the retained display identity; preserve cached data through the supported enabled option and restore normal freshness when the surface opens again. On retained routes, the supported subscribed option can release that observer and cancel an unused query through its consumed AbortSignal, while preserving another active observer. Keep late navigation scoped to a distinct visit; a simple focused boolean can revive an earlier result after leaving and returning. Shared account reconciliation may still be needed after view blur. Refreshing a URL does not prove native image display because transport and decoding can fail independently; do not add a global refetch loop to conceal an unexplained failure.
verification: load real content, background beyond the relevant TTL, resume without hot reload, and inspect refreshed data and actual media display. Repeat offline-to-online and with a delayed response. Exercise clock boundaries in focused tests and real suspension on both platforms.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, React Native 0.86 and TanStack Query 5.101.4 timer/query regressions; recheck on upgrades.

entries.title: Elapsed time survives suspended timers
entries.trigger: time-limited permissions, drafts, cached measurements and retry eligibility.
entries.mechanism: suspension delays a scheduled callback, leaving an apparently ready state after its underlying authorization or measurement has expired.
entries.prevention: compare the authoritative timestamp when resuming and immediately before the protected action. Keep data freshness distinct from presentation state. Follow the feature's existing deadline.
verification: just-before, exact-boundary and after-boundary tests; background across that boundary; missing/future timestamps when those states can originate from persistence or a platform callback.
boundaries: 2026-09-06; this is an elapsed-time invariant, not a recommendation for a particular TTL.

entries.title: System calendar settings are runtime inputs
entries.trigger: an app caches Intl date/time formatters or keeps screens mounted across Settings.
entries.mechanism: an Intl formatter retains the timezone selected when it was constructed. A locale default also does not represent the device's explicit 12/24-hour preference.
entries.prevention: track current calendar/clock settings with the platform's supported API, invalidate affected formatter snapshots and notify retained consumers. Refresh on foreground where native change events are incomplete. Preserve explicit app choices and do not rewrite stored timestamps. Native timezone identifiers are not automatically valid Intl option values; use supported runtime resolution rather than inventing a timezone parser.
verification: change timezone across a date boundary and switch system hour format while app language stays unchanged. Resume the same mounted screen; verify explicit app overrides too. Real Intl checks can establish snapshot semantics, but platform event delivery needs a native device.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Intl and Expo Localization 57.0.1; Android configuration events and iOS significant time events were inspected. Physical Settings behavior remains adopting-project acceptance.

entries.title: Reconcile external state even when server values are unchanged
entries.trigger: a native badge or other external projection can change independently of query data.
entries.mechanism: a push overwrote the badge, but an identical server response did not rerun the correction. Two updates can share the same millisecond timestamp; it is not a unique success token.
entries.prevention: observe successful response identity through supported query options when the external projection needs reconciliation. For a small JSON projection, disabling structural sharing locally preserves each parsed response. A user command that already applies an optimistic canonical projection should mirror that same value to native state directly, then let command settlement and the authoritative refresh converge failures or concurrent changes. Keep account ownership and failed-read behavior explicit. Do not put a timeout-and-retry race around a non-cancelable native write without proving its completion ordering; a timed-out old write can otherwise overwrite a newer value later.
verification: overwrite the external projection, then fetch identical canonical values under a fixed clock. Test zero/nonzero, failed fetch, invalidation, resume and account replacement. Native effects still need device evidence; a mocked badge call proves only application orchestration.
boundaries: 2026-09-09, TanStack Query 5.101.4 / React 19.2 / Expo Notifications 57.0.17. This exception is for projections that need every successful response, not a reason to disable structural sharing throughout an app.

entries.title: Reapply native state after the permission transition which enables it
entries.trigger: a platform can report retained native state while rejecting writes until a separate permission is granted, including an iOS app-icon badge retained across reinstall.
entries.mechanism: the server and local inbox both reported zero and the client requested native zero, but the clean install had never requested notification permission. Expo returned an unsupported write and an accepted badge-only push did not remove the visible SpringBoard number.
entries.prevention: read native state and permission as separate facts. When a positive retained value conflicts with an authoritative online zero, explain the recovery before requesting permission. Reapply the unchanged canonical value at the exact permission transition; do not rely on a structurally equal query result to rerun an effect, and do not change unrelated category choices.
verification: reproduce a retained badge on a clean install with undecided permission; prove no prompt while offline or before an authoritative read, separate rationale receipts, explicit allow/deny behavior and the post-grant zero write. Mocked orchestration remains separate from a physical app-icon result.
boundaries: 2026-09-09, iOS / Expo Notifications 57.0.17. Physical acceptance of the replacement OTA remains required.

entries.title: External screens are part of the operation lifecycle
entries.trigger: camera, photo picker, Settings, permission prompts or other external activities.
entries.mechanism: background/inactive events are mistaken for cancellation, returned data belongs to a stale draft, or returning from Settings leaves a cached permission/freshness state unchanged.
entries.prevention: separate the native handoff's pending/result state from app focus. Recheck the relevant permission or freshness on return and preserve the result while retrying only the failed step. A notification route can be accepted while a platform camera remains visibly above the app; the public ImagePicker API does not provide a safe command to dismiss that external screen. Let its result or cancellation return normally before exposing the already-selected application route. Opening Settings can itself reject on both native platforms. Catch that documented failure, retain the previous user choice, show localized retry guidance and keep the action available. Derive route behavior from the current user flow, not from an old embedded-camera implementation.
verification: allow, deny, permanently deny, cancel, retake, background, process termination and returning from Settings. Also enter from a notification while the external camera is visible, then cancel and complete the capture flow. Check the real camera/picker result and screen order on both platforms.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, React Native 0.86 and Expo SDK 57. System UI and returned files are platform-owned.

entries.title: Cold notification entry is different from a warm navigation push
entries.trigger: notifications, widgets or links can launch a terminated application.
entries.mechanism: routing precedes account/bootstrap readiness, or Back assumes a previous screen that a cold-start stack does not contain.
entries.prevention: wait for authentication restoration before choosing an account gate, then respect the existing readiness and recipient gates. A query disabled by an unmet account prerequisite can remain pending without representing visible loading. Provide the product-approved Back destination when cold entry has no previous route, use the navigator's supported fallback behavior, and avoid repeating the same navigation on subsequent renders.
verification: foreground, background and terminated entry; signed-out and wrong-account entry; expired/deleted target; Back after direct entry. Record the exact signed build when testing push.
boundaries: 2026-09-06, Expo Router SDK 57; routing APIs and notification capabilities are version-sensitive.

entries.title: A synthetic binary fixture cannot establish native file compatibility
entries.trigger: image preparation, binary validation or transport changes replace a platform or maintained-library path with application code.
entries.mechanism: a handwritten parser or second byte rewrite passes simplified fixtures but rejects a valid native photo; one deployed caller can retain the old shared helper after another caller is fixed. Unit success conceals the installed-client failure.
entries.prevention: start with the supported native encoder and a maintained format reader. Treat upload MIME metadata as untrusted and apply the library's supported format restriction before invoking a parser for a narrower contract; a format check after parsing is too late. A rejected promise cannot interrupt a synchronous parser loop, so reproduce malformed-file hangs in bounded isolated processes. Preserve actual failing and valid files, trace every shared-helper consumer, and deploy compatible callers together. When bespoke code regresses, evaluate restoring the supported path.
verification: exercise real output from each affected platform, expected dimensions/bytes and downstream storage/restore. Include malformed alternate formats in a bounded process and prove the restricted parser never enters the unsupported synchronous loop. Simplified fixtures cover individual branches only. After rollout, verify the deployed shared dependency for every entry point and repeat the original failing flow.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Expo SDK 57 ImageManipulator and image-size 2.0.2 with format restriction. Recheck encoders/readers on upgrades; the referenced parser is archived, so maintenance risk remains separate from the demonstrated mitigation. Using a dimension reader does not prove metadata removal or full image decoding.

entries.title: Round crop geometry before clamping its bounds
entries.trigger: fractional zoom is converted into integer-pixel crop rectangles for native imaging.
entries.mechanism: independently rounding size and origin made a 101-pixel image crop end at pixel 102 at 2x zoom. Algebraic bounds before rounding did not guarantee valid native parameters.
entries.prevention: round the crop size first, then constrain the origin using that same integer size.
verification: odd square/portrait/landscape dimensions, bottom/right edges, fractional zoom and centered controls; separately save these crops through the real native image API.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Expo SDK 57 crop API and installed Android/iOS source. Geometry reproduced in unit tests; actual device decoding/encoding acceptance remains separate.

entries.title: Optimistic sending state must follow the native handoff it claims
entries.trigger: a user starts a network command and may background the app immediately after its optimistic pending state appears.
entries.mechanism: the message surface rendered `Sending...` before session lookup and the ordinary Edge fetch began. Backgrounding at that point could suspend progress, and the recipient observed the message only when the sender returned and sent another one.
entries.prevention: if normal background delivery is a product invariant, start a supported native background transfer before publishing the pending row. Retain the native task through the existing lifecycle owner and preserve the command's stable identity. Do not add a foreground resend, generic retry scheduler or durable outbox unless offline/process-death recovery is separately required.
verification: assert the native task starts before pending UI publication, its exact request stays owner-bound, and terminal success/failure releases native resources and transient files. Source tests do not establish physical background execution; verify the signed artifact on each target platform.
boundaries: 2026-09-10, Expo FileSystem 57.0.6, React Native 0.86.3, and an application message-send path.
